data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Independently operated services are more resilient only when the marginal independence of their operators exceeds the independence gain of intra-system replication; distinguishing true independence requires computing the divergence between na\u00efve and causally conditioned (operator-conditioned) failure copulas.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the operator population converges on a single homogeneous software stack (monoculture), the operator-level common cause can dominate and the decentralized network becomes more fragile.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large internal service uses diverse, administratively isolated replication (independent operators within the firm, different vendors, staged rollouts), it may achieve true component independence and out-resilience the network.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the small services all depend on a single shared resource (e.g., a common DNS or identity provider) whose failure induces correlated outages, the claimed independence is an illusion.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A large service that internally replicates components often does so using the same operator, playbook, supply chain, and update cadence, creating latent shared causes (e.g., a single faulty rollout or single upstream vendor outage) that make the replicas' failures conditionally dependent rather than independent. A decentralized network distributes operator-level causal paths, so unless an operator-level common cause binds the nodes, their failure copula should be closer to the independence copula. The evidentiary discriminator is to compare the observed joint failure distribution against the same distribution conditioned on operator-level factors (deployment pipeline, cloud provider, administrative domain). If conditioning substantially changes the copula\u2014increasing tail dependence or shifting the joint failure probability\u2014the failures were merely apparently uncorrelated; if it does not, they are genuinely independent.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
